payload.task_text:
Our company is preparing for the annual compensation review and the VP of HR has asked for a detailed comparison of our internal salary data against published industry benchmarks. We have an industry benchmarking service that provides salary data through a REST API endpoint at http://localhost:30201/api/benchmarks.json which returns benchmark salary information for seven departments including average salary, median salary, and percentile ranges.

We also maintain our own employee records in the company data warehouse with salary information for approximately 50,000 employees across seven departments: R&D, Finance, Operations, Sales, HR, Support, and Engineering.

Please start by fetching the industry benchmark data from the API endpoint. Then pull the actual employee salary data from the data warehouse, grouped by department. The employee data resides in the HR_ANALYTICS database, PUBLIC schema, EMPLOYEES table — the per-employee annual salary is in the SALARY column and the department in the DEPARTMENT column. For each department, compute the average salary, median salary, minimum salary, maximum salary, and total headcount directly from these raw employee records; do not rely on any precomputed summaries, insights, or the SALARY_HISTORY table, which are not authoritative for this analysis.

Create an Excel file called "HR_Salary_Benchmark.xlsx" in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be called "Industry Benchmarks" and contain the benchmark data retrieved from the API, with columns for Department, Benchmark_Avg_Salary, Benchmark_Median_Salary, Benchmark_P25, and Benchmark_P75. The second sheet should be called "Internal Data" and include columns for Department, Internal_Avg_Salary, Internal_Median_Salary, Min_Salary, Max_Salary, and Headcount, populated with actual data from the data warehouse. The third sheet should be called "Variance Analysis" and contain columns for Department, Benchmark_Avg, Internal_Avg, Variance_Amount (the difference between internal average and benchmark average), and Variance_Pct (the percentage difference calculated as the variance amount divided by the benchmark average, multiplied by 100). A positive variance means our salaries are above benchmark and negative means below benchmark.

Next, create a Word document called "Salary_Benchmark_Report.docx" in the workspace. This executive summary should include a title, an overview paragraph describing the purpose of the analysis, a section listing each department with its benchmark versus internal average salary and the variance percentage, a section identifying which departments are above benchmark and which are below, and a concluding recommendation paragraph.

Finally, send an email to vp-hr@company.com with the subject "Annual Salary Benchmark Analysis Report". The sender address is fixed by the email environment; only the recipient and subject matter. The body should summarize the key findings, mentioning the department with the largest positive variance (most above benchmark) and the department with the largest negative variance (most below benchmark).

Save all output files to the workspace directory.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must list the task-visible workspace, read every relevant reference in read-only mode, and freeze the seven department labels and calculation rules. It must then call `fetch_json(url="http://localhost:30201/api/benchmarks.json")` and run the independent set-based aggregation over `HR_ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEES` in the same native-parallel response. The SQL branch must compute count, average, median, minimum, and maximum directly from employee `SALARY` grouped by `DEPARTMENT`, plus grand-total headcount; it must not read `SALARY_HISTORY` or a precomputed summary. Require exactly seven rows from each source, join by the original department labels, compute signed variance amount and percentage from unrounded inputs, identify deterministic largest positive/negative variances, and freeze one canonical seven-row table. In the same orchestration response that launches Wave 1, the main agent must search Sent mail for the exact recipient `vp-hr@company.com` and subject `Annual Salary Benchmark Analysis Report`, send exactly one message only if no exact match exists using the frozen largest-positive and largest-negative departments, and retain its message ID. This email branch must run natively in parallel with both artifact writers.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own HR_Salary_Benchmark.xlsx exactly once. Build the exact "Industry Benchmarks", "Internal Data", and "Variance Analysis" sheets from the frozen table with the original columns and literal values, apply the requested rounding, read the workbook back, and return its path plus sheet, row, department, and arithmetic checks. Do not create the Word document or send email.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own Salary_Benchmark_Report.docx exactly once. From the same frozen table, create the requested executive overview, department-by-department benchmark/internal/variance section, above-versus-below lists, and recommendation paragraph. Read the document back and return its path plus heading, department, and extrema checks. Do not create the workbook or send email.

After Wave 1, the main agent must cross-check both artifacts against the canonical table, read the retained message back, and verify that it names the same largest positive and largest negative variance departments. It must preserve unrelated messages, complete every undelegated requirement, and verify all outputs before ending.

Requirements:
- Write STATIC numeric values (do not use formulas) so that any reader sees the numbers.
- All numbers must be stored as numbers, not text strings.

Build HR salary benchmark Excel

Create a Word document at exactly this absolute path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-fetch-sf-hr-benchmark-excel-word/workspace/Salary_Benchmark_Report.docx

Purpose: an executive summary for the VP of HR comparing internal salaries against industry benchmark data (source: National Compensation Survey 2025, fetched from the company benchmarking API; internal data: 50,000 employee salary records from the HR_ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEES warehouse table).

Required structure (use headings for the section titles; keep it professional and readable):

1. Title (a document title such as "Annual Salary Benchmark Analysis Report" plus a short subtitle line mentioning it was prepared for the VP of HR).
2. An "Overview" section with one paragraph describing the purpose of the analysis (annual compensation review, comparing internal average salaries by department against published industry benchmark averages, based on 50,000 employee records across seven departments, benchmark data from the National Compensation Survey 2025).
3. A "Departmental Comparison" section listing EACH of the seven departments with its benchmark average salary vs internal average salary and the variance percentage. Present this as a table AND/OR as a short paragraph/bullet per department — either way every one of the seven departments must appear with its benchmark average, internal average, and variance percentage.
4. A "Departments Above and Below Benchmark" section that explicitly identifies which departments are above benchmark (positive variance) and which are below benchmark (negative variance).
5. A "Recommendations" section with a concluding recommendation paragraph.

Exact data to use (variance = internal average minus benchmark average; variance % = variance / benchmark average * 100):

| Department | Benchmark Avg | Internal Avg | Variance Amount | Variance % |
| Engineering | $62,000 | $58,991.61 | -$3,008.39 | -4.85% |
| Finance | $55,000 | $57,878.19 | +$2,878.19 | +5.23% |
| HR | $54,000 | $58,920.45 | +$4,920.45 | +9.11% |
| Operations | $56,000 | $57,808.74 | +$1,808.74 | +3.23% |
| R&D | $61,000 | $57,905.93 | -$3,094.07 | -5.07% |
| Sales | $57,000 | $58,864.79 | +$1,864.79 | +3.27% |
| Support | $52,000 | $58,400.48 | +$6,400.48 | +12.31% |

Above benchmark: Finance, HR, Operations, Sales, Support.
Below benchmark: Engineering, R&D.
Largest positive variance: Support (+12.31%, +$6,400.48 above benchmark). Largest negative variance: R&D (-5.07%, -$3,094.07 below benchmark).

The recommendation paragraph should note that five of seven departments pay above benchmark (Support most notably), so the focus should be on cost containment and targeted review in over-market departments, while Engineering and R&D are below benchmark and risk attrition, so targeted adjustments there are warranted (e.g., prioritize R&D and Engineering salary adjustments in the coming cycle, especially for high-performing and hard-to-replace roles).

Additional context you may use: internal headcount is roughly 7,000-7,300 per department (Engineering 7,096; Finance 7,148; HR 7,077; Operations 7,120; R&D 7,083; Sales 7,232; Support 7,244), and internal median salaries are Engineering $53,594; Finance $52,987; HR $53,656; Operations $52,293; R&D $52,404; Sales $53,488; Support $52,943.

Use USD currency formatting in the text. Do not add a table of contents.

After saving, read the document text back and verify that the title, all five sections, all seven departments with their numbers, the above/below lists, and the recommendation paragraph are present and accurate. Fix anything wrong before finishing.

Report back the final file path and a confirmation of the verified content (list the sections and confirm each department's variance percentage appears correctly).
